audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Iconium signs/opposition, Lystra healing, Zeus/Hermes misunderstanding, living Divine speech, stoning Paul, strengthening disciples, appointing elders.

verses.restored: It happened in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Judeans and spoke in such a way that a great multitude of both Judeans and Greeks trusted.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake, that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed.

modern.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος.

verses.restored: But the Judeans who were disobedient stirred up and embittered the souls/lives of the nations against the siblings.

familiar.text: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles, and made their minds evil affected against the brethren.

modern.text: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ⸀ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.

verses.restored: Therefore they remained a considerable time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who was bearing witness to the word of his grace by giving signs and wonders to happen through their hands.

familiar.text: Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of his grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

modern.text: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.

original.text: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ⸀τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: The multitude of the city was divided: some were with the Judeans, and some with the apostles.

familiar.text: But the multitude of the city was divided: and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

modern.text: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.

original.text: ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις.

verses.restored: When an impulse arose from both the nations and Judeans, with their rulers, to mistreat and stone them,

familiar.text: And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews with their rulers, to use them despitefully, and to stone them,

modern.text: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς,

verses.restored: becoming aware, they fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region,

familiar.text: They were ware of it, and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lieth round about:

modern.text: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,

original.text: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον,

verses.restored: and there they were announcing the good news.

familiar.text: And there they preached the gospel.

modern.text: where they continued to preach the gospel. The Visit to Lystra and Derbe

original.text: κἀκεῖ ⸂εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν⸃.

verses.restored: In Lystra a certain man was sitting, powerless in the feet, lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.

familiar.text: And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked:

modern.text: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.

original.text: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ⸂ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις⸃ τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο, χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ⸀αὐτοῦ, ὃς οὐδέποτε ⸀περιεπάτησεν.

verses.restored: This one heard Paul speaking. Paul, looking intently at him and seeing that he had trust to be saved/healed,

familiar.text: The same heard Paul speak: who stedfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,

modern.text: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.

original.text: οὗτος ⸀ἤκουσεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος· ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ⸂ἔχει πίστιν⸃ τοῦ σωθῆναι

verses.restored: said with a great voice, Stand upright on your feet. And he leaped up and began walking.

familiar.text: Said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.

modern.text: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.

original.text: εἶπεν ⸀μεγάλῃ φωνῇ· Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ⸀ὀρθός· καὶ ⸀ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει.

verses.restored: The crowds, seeing what Paul did, lifted their voice in Lycaonian, saying, The gods, becoming like humans, have come down to us.

familiar.text: And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.

modern.text: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”

original.text: οἵ ⸀τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ⸀ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες· Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς

verses.restored: They were calling Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, because he was the leading speaker.

familiar.text: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.

modern.text: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.

original.text: ἐκάλουν τε ⸀τὸν Βαρναβᾶν Δία, τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου.

verses.restored: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was before the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates, wanting to sacrifice with the crowds.

familiar.text: Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people.

modern.text: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.

original.text: ὅ ⸀τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς ⸀πόλεως ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν.

verses.restored: But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, hearing this, tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying out

familiar.text: Which when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of, they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,

modern.text: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,

original.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Παῦλος, διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια ⸀αὐτῶν ⸀ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες

verses.restored: and saying, Men, why do you do these things? We also are humans of like suffering with you, announcing good news to you to turn from these empty things to the living Divine, who made heaven and earth and sea and all things in them.

familiar.text: And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein:

modern.text: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

original.text: καὶ λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες, τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε; καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ ⸀θεὸν ζῶντα ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς·

verses.restored: In past generations he allowed all the nations to walk in their ways,

familiar.text: Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.

modern.text: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.

original.text: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν·

verses.restored: yet he did not leave himself without witness, doing good, giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.

familiar.text: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

modern.text: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

original.text: ⸀καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον ⸀αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ⸀ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ⸀ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Saying these things, with difficulty they restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.

familiar.text: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the people, that they had not done sacrifice unto them.

modern.text: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.

original.text: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: But Judeans came from Antioch and Iconium, and persuading the crowds, they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, supposing him to have died.

familiar.text: And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.

modern.text: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.

original.text: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, ⸀νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι.

verses.restored: But when the disciples surrounded him, rising, he entered the city. The next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.

familiar.text: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.

modern.text: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe. Strengthening the Disciples

original.text: κυκλωσάντων δὲ ⸂τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν⸃ ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν. καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρναβᾷ εἰς Δέρβην.

verses.restored: Having announced the good news to that city and made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

familiar.text: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,

modern.text: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

original.text: Εὐαγγελισάμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ ⸀εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ ⸁εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,

verses.restored: strengthening the souls/lives of the disciples, encouraging them to remain in the trust, and saying that through many pressures it is necessary for us to enter the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.

modern.text: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.

original.text: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει καὶ ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Appointing elders for them in every assembly, with prayer and fasting, they entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had trusted.

familiar.text: And when they had ordained them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed.

modern.text: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

original.text: χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς ⸂κατʼ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους⸃ προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν.

verses.restored: Passing through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia.

familiar.text: And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

modern.text: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

original.text: καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς ⸀τὴν Παμφυλίαν,

verses.restored: Speaking the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

familiar.text: And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia:

modern.text: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

original.text: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν,

verses.restored: From there they sailed away to Antioch, from where they had been handed over to the grace of the Divine for the work they had fulfilled.

familiar.text: And thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.

modern.text: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed.

original.text: κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν.

verses.restored: Arriving and gathering the assembly, they reported all that the Divine had done with them, and that he had opened a door of trust to the nations.

familiar.text: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all that God had done with them, and how he had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles.

modern.text: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

original.text: παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ⸀ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως.

verses.restored: They remained no little time with the disciples.

familiar.text: And there they abode long time with the disciples.

modern.text: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.

original.text: διέτριβον ⸀δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς.
